newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares fall, Kuwaitis buy up stock.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares fall, Kuwaitis buy up stock.

text.p: Shares on the Amman stock exchange fell 0.53 percent on Sunday in trade dominated by the sale of five percent of the stock of Jordan Kuwait Bank to Kuwaiti investors.

Abdul-Mutallib Abu Hijleh, who brokered the sale of the 500,000 shares, priced at 4.00 dinars each, said it had passed a controlling stake in the bank to Kuwaiti investors opposed to a merger with or takeover by Bank of Jordan.
The struggle for control of Jordan Kuwait Bank has brought the bank's stock into the limelight in recent weeks as one of the busiest shares on the market.

On Sunday it accounted for over two million dinars worth of trade, or two thirds of the entire turnover on the Amman bourse. It fell by 0.20 dinars to 3.77 dinars, helping push the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index down 0.53 percent to 159.96 points.

Abu Hijleh said Kuwaiti investors now hold over 48 percent of Jordan Kuwait Bank's stock, more than enough to hold a strong majority at an extraordinary meeting of shareholders next month called to discuss the bank's future. Only around 70 percent of shareholders are expected to turn up.
"Today's transaction will ensure that the merger plan does not go ahead," he said.
Overall 36 shares fell on Sunday and only seven rose. Another seven were traded but closed unchanged.
Some brokers said comments by Deputy Prime Minister Jawad Anani on Saturday that the state would offer government employees discounted shares in its privatisation programme had hit market sentiment.
They said there was too little cash liquidity on the market to soak up any large offerings of shares.

"They took it negatively, but it should have been positive news," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Investments. "The liquidity is an artificial problem. Most institutions have a very big liquidity available to them."
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.59 percent to 80.97 points, 2.90 percent down from the start of the year.
